reason: Driven in Chromium with forcedColors:active at 390x844 and 1440x960 on both grounds, painted pixels decoded from the screenshot buffer. The core of the finding reproduces exactly. LOADING: the four .b-skel slabs sit at [15,65,107,86], [20,161,227,26], [20,195,188,23], [20,230,92,15] at 390 and [541,133,107,86], [546,229,227,26], [546,263,188,23], [546,298,92,15] at 1440; unforced they paint [231,231,231] on paper and [41,41,41] on ink, and under a forced palette every one of them paints [255,255,255] on a [255,255,255] ground, identical on paper and ink, at both widths - zero contrast, no border, computed box-shadow none. The frame the audience is left with is the plan name, a 180px void, the today rule, 'TODAY IS 16 JULY' and one sentence; screenshotted side by side against the unforced frame, the forced one reads as an empty plan, not as a plan arriving. loading-slow flattens the same way. EDITING: .b-item[data-editing="true"] .b-copy at [130,103,240,71] (390) and [710,676,534,79] (1440) paints [241,241,241]/[31,31,31] unforced and [255,255,255] on [255,255,255] forced, on both grounds and both widths; computed box-shadow is 'none' in forced colours, so the 12px halo cannot stand in - confirmed, not merely asserted. owner-undone flattens identically ([130,201,...] / [710,515,...]). Screenshotted at 390, the edited row is pixel-indistinguishable from the row above it: same title weight, same mono date, same Edit. And the gate really does not cover this - interaction-check.mjs opens a forced palette only at 2113 (owner-flight), 3146 (visibility segment) and 3233 (the lead ring), never on loading or on an open editor. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENTS DO NOT KILL IT. (a) 'A skeleton is decoration and a forced palette is a legibility mode' fails on this artifact's own written doctrine: b.css:1585-1607 states 'a forced palette may repaint any fill but cannot flatten a shape' and honours it for .b-tick, the chosen segment, the lead ring and the crowded leader (b.css:242). A skeleton is the one object in the product that is nothing BUT shape - repaint its fill and there is nothing left, so the rule applies to it with more force, not less. Three objects obey the house rule and the loading frame does not; that inconsistency is what a 9.5 costs. (b) 'The panel's position and aria make the edited row obvious' is partly true and does not save it: the panel is aria-labelled 'Editing Send the invitations', the row's .b-grab carries aria-expanded=true/aria-controls=b-edit, and the panel's first field visibly holds 'Send the invitations' with '8 August 2026' under it. But at 1440 the panel sits at [186,597] and the row at [710,676] - a 520px gap across two columns - and the answer to 'which of these seven rows am I changing' becomes 'read every title and match it against a field'. WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG, and it is wrong twice. (1) .b-bubble is NOT flattened. It already declares border: 1px solid var(--ink-10) (b.css:1063), which a forced palette repaints to CanvasText: measured on paper and ink at 390 and 1440, the bubble paints a [0,0,0] hairline at [16,279,300,49]/[456,351,300,49] with its 16px radius intact. One third of the finding's premise is false and the third rule of its fix is a no-op. (2) The fix's own geometry is wrong at desktop. Driven verbatim, outline-offset: 12px on the edited .b-copy is clipped on the RIGHT at 1440 by .b-plan (overflow:auto, box [586,231,668,664], so the clip edge is x=1254 and the ring wants x=1256): the ring paints on three sides only, left/top/bottom black at 13/13/12 and nothing at all on the right, on both grounds. 10px is clipped too; 9px and below close all four sides at both widths (L=10 R=9 T=10 B=9). The finding's other numbers hold - documentElement.scrollHeight is 2574 before and after at 390 and 1067 at 1440, the skel rects are byte-identical with the border added because shell.css:183 sets box-sizing: border-box globally, and there is no collision with the focus ring, which is on .b-edit. CONFIRMED as a correction, not a build: two rules inside a block that already exists, in system colours the block already uses, with the bubble rule dropped and the offset closed.
sharpenedFix: Two rules, not three, at the foot of the existing @media (forced-colors: active) block in b.css. Drop the .b-bubble rule entirely - it already carries border: 1px solid var(--ink-10) and a forced palette already repaints that to a CanvasText hairline (measured [0,0,0] on both grounds at both widths), so the proposed rule buys nothing and only adds a line to maintain. Keep `.b-skel { background: Canvas; border: 1px solid CanvasText; }` verbatim; box-sizing is redundant because shell.css:183 already sets border-box globally, and the four rects stay exactly [15,65,107,86], [20,161,227,26], [20,195,188,23], [20,230,92,15] at 390 with the hairline painting on every edge. Change the second rule to `.b-item[data-editing="true"] .b-copy { outline: 1px solid CanvasText; outline-offset: 9px; }` - at 12px (and at 10px) the ring's right edge falls outside .b-plan's overflow:auto clip at x=1254 and the row gets a three-sided bracket at 1440 on both grounds; at 9px all four sides paint at 390 and 1440, the left edge stays 6px clear of the .b-tick at x=107..114, and scrollHeight is unchanged (2574 at 390, 1067 at 1440). Then extend interaction-check.mjs so a forced palette is opened on loading and on an open editor as well as owner-flight, asserting a non-Canvas edge on each .b-skel and a painted ring on the edited row, on both grounds.
